reasons: The level list is duplicated in another file.

terms.meaning: A small saved-data store in the browser, kept per site and per device.
A choice where only one option can be selected at a time.
A way to pass a value down through many components without naming it at each step.
A React tool that keeps a component up to date with a value kept outside React, such as browser storage.

sections.name: File setup, DEPTHS, Depth, Ctx
sections.title: Levels, key and default
sections.what: Declares the three depth levels, a type that matches them, the storage key name, and a default context of quick.
sections.why: Likely reason: one fixed list keeps the labels and saved values consistent.
sections.watch_out: Changing the storage key name makes everyone's saved choice disappear.

sections.name: listeners, isDepth
sections.title: Listeners and level check
sections.what: Keeps a set of listeners that are told when the choice changes, a memory copy of the choice, and a check that a value is a real level.
sections.why: The code comment says memory keeps the choice when storage is blocked.
sections.watch_out: The memory copy resets on a full page reload when storage is blocked.

sections.name: read
sections.title: Reading the saved level
sections.what: Reads the level from storage and falls back to the memory copy if storage fails or holds an unknown value.
sections.why: The code comment says storage can be blocked, so failures are handled quietly.

sections.name: subscribe
sections.title: Subscribing to changes
sections.what: Lets a component be told about changes, both from this page and from other browser tabs.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps several tabs in agreement.
sections.watch_out: The cleanup function must remove both listeners, or the page leaks memory.

sections.name: choose
sections.title: Saving a new choice
sections.what: Saves the new level, updates the memory copy, and tells every listener.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps storage, memory and the screen in step.
sections.watch_out: Storage failures are ignored, so a blocked device shows no error to the reader.

sections.name: DepthProvider
sections.title: Depth radio buttons
sections.what: Draws the three radio buttons with the chosen one selected, and passes the chosen level to the children.
sections.why: Likely reason: the switch and the text must agree, so the switch sits above the text.
sections.watch_out: The server fallback always uses quick, so the first draw may show quick before the saved choice applies.

sections.name: DepthText
sections.title: Depth text
sections.what: Shows the paragraphs for the chosen level and announces changes politely to screen readers.
sections.why: The code comment says all three texts are rendered on the server, so switching is instant.
sections.watch_out: Each level needs its own text list; a missing level shows nothing.

summary: A radio button switch that lets readers choose how detailed the Desk text is, and remembers the choice on this device.
purpose: Lets readers choose Quick, Tactical or Analyst depth for each Desk item.
why: The code comment says the choice is kept in browser storage per device, and in memory when storage is blocked.
how: Saves the choice in local storage and in a memory copy. Reads the saved value on render, listens for changes from other tabs, and draws three radio buttons. A provider passes the chosen level to the text beneath it.
inputs: Labels from the parent page, the saved level in browser storage, and clicks on the radio buttons.
outputs: Three radio buttons and the chosen paragraphs shown by DepthText.
risks: The three levels are listed here and also in the domain service, so the lists must match. If storage is blocked, the choice lasts only for the visit.
debug: If the choice does not stick, check the local storage key alterego.desk.depth. If the text does not change, check that the labels and texts use the same level names. If tabs do not sync, check the storage listener.
